title: Starter pack: 30m inertia busters + price anchors
content:
Objective:
Create a concise ‘starter pack’ messaging and microcopy set that reduces developer inertia and frames Hosted API pricing in developer-friendly terms. Target 30-minute integration (curl + Node/Python snippet) -> obvious next step (save tokens, upgrade, try dedicated).

Guiding principles (developer-first):
- Make success immediate: ship a working request in <30m, with observable latency/cost.
- Transparent economics: show per-token and per-request cost early, include a ‘cost preview’ toggle in quickstart.
- Low cognitive load: one-page quickstart, one curl, one SDK snippet, one sample prompt template.
- Trust and safety hooks: short note on data handling + link to privacy/SLA for teams evaluating production.
- Next-step clarity: callouts to ‘scale options’ (Dedicated, Private) with concrete migration bullets.

Quickstart angles (three microtracks):
1) Rapid prototype (0->demo): Curl + web demo
   - Objective: get a prototype response inline with one curl and one HTML demo.
   - Microcopy: "Try a response in your terminal — 1 sample curl, 60s to see results."
   - Steps: signup -> API key -> curl example -> embed in a static page -> share link.
   - Cost framing: "This demo uses ~X tokens (~$0.00Y). Free credits included."

2) Productize (POC -> commit): SDK + telemetry
   - Objective: show typical production touchpoints: long responses, streaming, error handling, usage breakdown.
   - Microcopy: "Add the SDK, enable streaming, and get token-level cost breakdown in Console."
   - Steps: install SDK -> snippet with streaming handler -> enable quota alert -> check Console for token & latency charts.
   - Cost framing: "Estimate: 1M tokens ~= $Z — toggle quantized model to reduce cost by ~30% for non-critical outputs."

3) Enterprise eval (security + throughput)
   - Objective: highlight Dedicated & Private as next steps — SLAs, VPC, KMS.
   - Microcopy: "Production-grade inference with reserved capacity and audit logs."
   - Steps: request a Dedicated trial -> sample throughput benchmark -> export audit log.

Developer-first value props (short bullets for hero + subtitle):
- Hero: "Hosted inference that devs actually ship with — low-latency, transparent pricing, predictable results."
- Supporting bullets: "One API, real-time streaming, instant metric feedback, built-in fallbacks when capacity matters."
- Quick trust stat: "Start serving in ~30m — or run a 1-hour POC with production SLA options."

Price-language variations to test (A/B candidates):
A) Straight numeric anchors
   - Microcopy: "Credits: get $50 to try. Pricing: $0.0008 / input token, $0.0012 / output token. Embeddings $0.0003 / vector."
B) Unit-first framing
   - Microcopy: "Most prototypes cost < $5/day. Estimate: 1M tokens ≈ $800."
C) Outcome framing (for product teams)
   - Microcopy: "Estimate the cost of a feature: 10k monthly calls at 200 tokens ≈ $X/month — trackable in Console."
D) Risk-minimizing (for enterprises)
   - Microcopy: "Reserve capacity with monthly commits to lock pricing and get latency SLAs."

Suggested microcopy for pricing CTA variants:
- Try: "Start free — get $50 in credits, no card for devs."
- Upgrade: "Commit for predictable throughput and 20% off unit price."
- Estimate tool: "Cost preview — upload a prompt set to see estimated monthly cost."

Competitive notes (concise scouting takeaways):
- Big cloud AI endpoints: strong on infrastructure reach but often opaque unit economics; angle: 'transparent token accounting + dev UX'
- LLM API platforms: ease of model access but varying reliability at scale; angle: 'SLA-backed runtime + fallbacks'
- Self-hosted runtimes: lowest marginal cost in some cases but long ops ramp; angle: 'same API across Hosted/Dedicated/Private to remove rewrite tax'

Rapid experiments (two-week sprints):
1) Onramp copy A/B test (homepage + email): Test unit-first vs outcome-first vs free-credit anchor. Metric: API key signups -> first 100 tokens used.
2) Pricing preview widget: Add cost-preview to quickstart (client-side calc from sample prompt). Metric: conversion from quickstart to repeat usage.
3) One-click demo (static app + embed): Gauge viral sharing; metric: demo-share rate and signups from shared demo.

Email / banner lines (short):
- Subject: "Ship an LLM feature in 30 minutes — $50 credits inside"
- Banner: "Prototype in terminal — no card required. Free developer credits."
- CTA buttons: "Try in 30m", "Estimate my cost", "Request Dedicated trial"

Objection handling (copy snippets):
- "What about price volatility?" -> "Lock unit price with Reserved/Dedicated plans; Console shows token-level trends so you can optimize."
- "Will this scale?" -> "SLA-backed Dedicated pools and smart routing keep latency stable under load."
- "What about data privacy?" -> "Hosted API supports customer-managed keys and enterprise Private deployments for sensitive workloads."

Landing page wire copy (scaffold):
- H1: "A hosted inference API engineers actually rely on"
- Subhead: "Fast to start, predictable to scale—streaming, observability, and the migration path to Dedicated or Private."
- Three cards: "Prototype (30m)", "Production (SLA)", "Private (VPC & KMS)" each with 1-line benefit and price anchor.

Metrics to track (initial 8 weeks):
- Time to first successful request (median)
- % of signups that use >10k tokens in 14 days (activation)
- Quickstart drop-off points (signup, key copy, curl run)
- Conversion to paid + average spend by cohort (free-credit vs card-on-file)

Next steps (action items):
- Design: build cost-preview widget and one-click HTML demo (owner: Marco).
- Engineering: create 30m quickstart repo with prerecorded short video + curl/snippets + cost-preview (owner: Sofia).
- Growth: draft 3 email variants for A/B (owner: Aisha).
- Prod marketing: produce single-page comparison vs typical cloud endpoints (owner: Ethan).

Notes and open questions:
- Decide default pricing phrasing on public docs: unit-first (tokens) vs outcome-first (feature/cost per 1M). Recommend starting unit-first for developer clarity and adding outcome calculators.
- Free-credit amount: $50 vs $100 (ops ask) — start $50 and run uplift test.
- Quickstart observability: show a tiny chart of token spend for the session — is this feasible in 30m build?

Appendix: sample curl + Node snippet (to be copy-edited into quickstart)
- curl: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -d '{"model":"rwd-small","input":"Summarize this text"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
- Node (pseudocode): import Redwood from '@redwood/ai'; const client = new Redwood({key: process.env.RW}); const stream = await client.chat.stream({model:'rwd-small', messages:[...]});

End of brief.

Revision history: created 2024-11-21 by Aisha; edits on 2024-12-03 added pricing alternatives and experiments.
